title: 4 ספרי ילדים שעוזרים לילדים לדבר על רגשות

stage.need: Putting a name to a feeling (angry, sad, scared, happy) and noticing what someone else feels. CDC's 3-year tips say to talk about the child's emotions and give words for them; by 4 years CDC lists 'Comforts others who are hurt or sad' and suggests helping the child learn about others' feelings and talking about fears. ZERO TO THREE recommends reading books about feelings and talking about the pictures.
stage.age_caveat: Milestones describe what most children do by an age, not a deadline, and the three books span official ages 2-4 and 4-6. Slide 2 says בסביבות; the caption repeats that some children talk about feelings early and some need more time.

dev_sources.title: Milestones by 3 Years
dev_sources.publisher: CDC, Learn the Signs. Act Early.
dev_sources.quote: Talk about your child's emotions and give him words to help him explain how he's feeling. / Read with your child. Ask questions, such as "What is happening in the picture?"
dev_sources.supports: CDC parent tip at 3 years: name the child's feelings and give him the words for them; while reading, ask what is happening in the picture. Supports slide 3 (naming a feeling from a picture) and slide 6 (asking which colour, i.e. which feeling). Caveat: these are parent tips, not milestones; read via WebFetch because the CDC server blocks direct downloads.

dev_sources.title: Milestones by 4 Years
dev_sources.publisher: CDC, Learn the Signs. Act Early.
dev_sources.quote: Comforts others who are hurt or sad, like hugging a crying friend / Help your child learn about others' feelings, and about positive ways to react. / Comfort your child if he is afraid and talk about his fears.
dev_sources.supports: Social/emotional milestone by 4 years: comforting others who are hurt or sad (slide 2). Parent tips: help the child learn about others' feelings (slide 4, guessing what Tali feels) and talk about his fears (slide 5, where was it scary). Caveat: CDC milestones are what most children (75% or more) do by that age.

dev_sources.title: 24-36 Months: Social-Emotional Development
dev_sources.quote: Teaching children the words for emotions is important because, over time, it gives children the ability to talk about their feelings instead of acting them out. / Read books about feelings and talk about the pictures: Which child looks mad? Which looks afraid?
dev_sources.supports: Emotion words help children talk about feelings instead of acting them out (slide 2, 'מילה לרגש יכולה לעזור לדבר עליו'); reading books about feelings and talking about the faces in the pictures (slides 2, 3 and 4). Caveat: the page is written for 24 to 36 months, the younger edge of this carousel's range; the advice is not age-limited but the source is about toddlers.

dev_sources.title: How to Help Your Child Develop Empathy
dev_sources.quote: In fact, labeling and validating difficult feelings actually helps children learn to handle them
dev_sources.supports: Naming hard feelings such as anger is part of how children learn to handle them, and the page links this to empathy for others with difficult feelings. Supports slide 4 (Tali's anger and how her cousin understands it). Caveat: read via WebFetch; the page does not itself recommend asking what a book character feels.

products.popularity_reasoning: Strong Israel-specific signal: Sifriyat Pijama distributed 118,300 copies to older kindergarten classes in 2019-2020, plus the book is in print at Tzomet Sfarim from an established Hebrew publisher. No bestseller-list placement found; I did not find it at Steimatzky.
products.developmental_relevance: Tali is angry and refuses to sit with the family at Grandma's meal, so she hides under the table; her cousin Shira joins her there and slowly brings her back, and later, when Grandma is angry, Tali knows how to help (Sifriyat Pijama parent note). The child practises guessing what Tali feels from her face and body and why, and then what helped. Sifriyat Pijama's own activities include 'לא תמיד קל לזהות את הרגשות של האחר' and 'לפעמים אני עצוב, ולפעמים אני שמחה – פעילות רגשות'.
products.parent_tip_source: Stop in the middle and ask 'איך טלי מרגישה עכשיו?'. Based on the Sifriyat Pijama activity titles 'לא תמיד קל לזהות את הרגשות של האחר' and 'לעיין באיורים', and on CDC's 4-year tip 'Help your child learn about others' feelings'. The exact question is my wording.
